summary: The note explains why governments are building National Cybersecurity Strategies (NCS) and how assessing the national cyber threat landscape informs them. It covers cyber hygiene, evolving threats, international benchmarking, AI/ML, critical infrastructure protection, public-private partnerships and workforce development, with several dated 2023 initiatives as examples.
one_line: Overview of National Cybersecurity Strategy components and threat landscape assessment, illustrated with September–December 2023 initiatives and expert statements.
key_facts: A National Cybersecurity Strategy (NCS) is a country's coordinated plan to improve digital security, protect against cyber attacks, and handle the aftermath of attacks that do occur.
NCS frameworks have evolved from mere guidelines to actionable frameworks that include government, private sector participation and public awareness as key pillars.
Common cyber hygiene practices include regular software updates, password management, back-ups of critical data, and employee training programs.

On September 15, 2023, Jane Smith, Director of Cybersecurity Education at the non-profit CyberGuardian, launched an initiative to introduce cyber hygiene modules into school curriculums across the globe.
Today's cyber threat landscape includes complex state-sponsored attacks, organized cybercrime, and sophisticated ransomware operations that can cripple entire national infrastructures.
On September 20, 2023, John Doe, advisor to the UN Cybersecurity Council, said threat assessment must anticipate future threats through comprehensive intelligence gathering and analysis.
National cyber incident response teams (CIRTs) and information-sharing platforms form the frontline of defense, enabling quick isolation and mitigation of threats.
On October 5, 2023, the Global Cybersecurity Alliance (GCA) unveiled a framework for countries to measure their cybersecurity initiatives against international best practices.
Countries can harmonize practices with international standards such as those from the ISO or NIST.
On October 12, 2023, ShieldTech CEO Emily Jones said AI "provides predictive insights that enable proactive measures against potential cyber threats."

The Cybersecurity Infrastructure Initiative, launched November 1, 2023 and led by the Ministry of Cyber Defense, mandates minimum cybersecurity standards across all critical infrastructure sectors, plus regular audits and stress testing.

On December 3, 2023, the government's cybersecurity agency and Tech Alliance, a consortium of leading technology companies, agreed to joint efforts in threat intelligence and mutual aid in cybersecurity incidents.
The Cyber Resilience Scholarship Fund, announced on December 10, 2023, invests in equipping the future workforce with cybersecurity skills.
